allii-arrange-figures.title: Set out the clay figures
allii-arrange-figures.description: Clay figures and tongue-shaped pieces are placed for the counter-ritual.

allii-seat-patient.title: Seat the patient toward the Sun-god
allii-seat-patient.description: The bewitched person sits facing the Sun-god.

allii-raise-vessel.title: Raise the vessel and figures
allii-raise-vessel.description: The Old Woman lifts a naktamu vessel together with the clay figures toward the Sun-god.

allii-return-address.title: Demand that the sorcery return
allii-return-address.description: The address to the Sun-god asks that the maker of the bewitchment carry it away.

allii-wind-wool.title: Wind coloured wool around the figures
allii-wind-wool.description: The Old Woman winds wool thread around the figures while naming the affliction she is returning.

allii-set-basket.title: Place the deposit beneath the bed
allii-set-basket.description: A prepared deposit of objects is set under the patient's bed.

allii-sleep-over.title: Sleep over the deposit
allii-sleep-over.description: The patient sleeps over the placed ritual objects.

allii-lift-at-dawn.title: Lift the deposit at daybreak
allii-lift-at-dawn.description: At first light, the Old Woman removes the bedside deposit and moves it over the patient.

allii-press-earth.title: Press earth against the patient
allii-press-earth.description: The Old Woman presses an earth clod against the patient while uttering a purification analogy.

allii-press-dough.title: Press dough against the patient
allii-press-dough.description: The Old Woman presses a lump of dough against the patient and speaks a life-giving analogy.

uhhamuwa-bring-ram.title: Bring a ram
uhhamuwa-bring-ram.description: A ram is driven up for the rite.

uhhamuwa-twist-wool.title: Twist the coloured wool
uhhamuwa-twist-wool.description: Blue, red, yellow-green, black and white wool are combined.

uhhamuwa-make-wreath.title: Make a wool wreath
uhhamuwa-make-wreath.description: The combined wool is made into a wreath or ring.

uhhamuwa-crown-ram.title: Adorn the ram
uhhamuwa-crown-ram.description: The wool wreath is placed on one ram.

uhhamuwa-lead-to-road.title: Lead the ram toward the enemy road
uhhamuwa-lead-to-road.description: The adorned ram is driven onto the road toward enemy territory.

uhhamuwa-appeal-over-ram.title: Address the hostile god
uhhamuwa-appeal-over-ram.description: An appeal presents the adorned ram and asks the god to be at peace with Ḫatti.

uhhamuwa-drive-away-ram.title: Drive the ram away
uhhamuwa-drive-away-ram.description: The crowned ram is sent into enemy territory.

uhhamuwa-bring-fodder-fat.title: Bring fodder and fat
uhhamuwa-bring-fodder-fat.description: Fodder for the god's horses and sheep fat are brought.

uhhamuwa-address-horses-chariot.title: Address the god about his horses
uhhamuwa-address-horses-chariot.description: The speech asks that the horses eat, the chariot be greased, and the god turn back toward his land.

uhhamuwa-bring-goat-sheep.title: Bring a goat and two sheep
uhhamuwa-bring-goat-sheep.description: A billy goat and two sheep are brought into the rite.

offer-goat.title: Offer a goat
offer-goat.description: Assign a goat to a deity as an offering.
offer-goat.matchRule: The named recipient differs between rituals; the shared task is offering a goat.

offer-sheep-to-sun-god.title: Offer a sheep to the Sun-god
offer-sheep-to-sun-god.description: Assign a sheep or ewe to the Sun-god.
offer-sheep-to-sun-god.matchRule: Both passages specify a sheep or ewe offered to the Sun-god.

slaughter-sheep.title: Slaughter sheep
slaughter-sheep.description: The prescribed killing of sheep or rams before cooking them.
slaughter-sheep.matchRule: Both texts prescribe slaughter of sheep. Ašḫella also slaughters goats.

cook-sheep-meat.title: Cook sheep meat
cook-sheep-meat.description: Cook flesh from the sheep slaughtered in the rite.
cook-sheep-meat.matchRule: The shared action is cooking sheep meat after slaughter.

uhhamuwa-bring-food-drink.title: Bring food and drink
uhhamuwa-bring-food-drink.description: Cheese, sour bread, wine, beer and fruit are brought, along with named vessels.

uhhamuwa-prepare-for-road-god.title: Prepare them for the road god
uhhamuwa-prepare-for-road-god.description: The gathered provisions are prepared for the god of the road.

ashella-prepare-ram.title: Prepare a ram
ashella-prepare-ram.description: Each army lord supplies a ram at dusk.

ashella-twist-wool.title: Twist three colours of wool
ashella-twist-wool.description: White, red and green wool are worked into a cord.

ashella-bind-ram.title: Bind the cord and rings to the ram
ashella-bind-ram.description: The cord and metal ornaments are fastened to the ram’s neck and horns.

ashella-tether-ram.title: Tether the ram before a tent
ashella-tether-ram.description: The adorned ram is tied in front of a tent for the night.

ashella-appeal.title: Ask the plague god to be appeased
ashella-appeal.description: The speaker asks the god responsible for the plague to accept the tethered rams.

ashella-release-rams.title: Release the rams at the enemy border
ashella-release-rams.description: The rams are led through camp and let loose at the enemy border.

ashella-wash-salt-water.title: Wash hands in salted water
ashella-wash-salt-water.description: Salt is mixed with water, and the participants wash their hands.

ashella-pass-between-fires.title: Pass between two fires
ashella-pass-between-fires.description: Two fires are lit, and the participants walk between them.

ashella-bring-pig.title: Bring a pig on the third day
ashella-bring-pig.description: A pig is driven to a different open place with a goat and ram.

ashella-offer-pig.title: Offer the pig to the plague god
ashella-offer-pig.description: The pig is offered with the goat and ram to the god responsible for the plague.

ashella-offer-bull.title: Offer a bull to the Storm-god
ashella-offer-bull.description: The bull is offered to the Storm-god.

ashella-offer-rams.title: Offer three sheep to all the gods
ashella-offer-rams.description: Three sheep are offered to all the gods.

pulisa-select-substitutes.title: Select a prisoner and a woman
pulisa-select-substitutes.description: A prisoner of war and a woman from the enemy land are chosen as substitutes.

pulisa-remove-king-garments.title: Remove the king’s festive clothes
pulisa-remove-king-garments.description: The king takes off his festive garments.

pulisa-dress-man.title: Clothe the man in the king’s garments
pulisa-dress-man.description: The prisoner receives the king’s festive garments.

pulisa-dress-woman.title: Clothe the woman in festive garments
pulisa-dress-woman.description: The woman is dressed in festive garments.

pulisa-address-man.title: Address the male deity
pulisa-address-man.description: The speaker offers the adorned man as a substitute and asks that he carry the plague away.

pulisa-address-woman.title: Address the female deity
pulisa-address-woman.description: The corresponding words are spoken to the woman concerning a female deity.

pulisa-bring-bull-ewe.title: Bring a bull and ewe
pulisa-bring-bull-ewe.description: A bull and ewe from the enemy land are brought forward.

pulisa-ring-bull.title: Fit rings at the bull’s ears
pulisa-ring-bull.description: The bull is fitted with ašuša-objects at its ears; their identification as rings is uncertain.

pulisa-draw-wool.title: Draw coloured wool from the king’s mouth
pulisa-draw-wool.description: Red, green, black and partly restored white wool are drawn out of the king’s mouth.

pulisa-address-bull.title: Offer the bull to the male deity
pulisa-address-bull.description: The speaker offers the bull as a substitute and asks it to carry the plague away.

pulisa-address-ewe.title: Offer the ewe to the female deity
pulisa-address-ewe.description: The ewe is brought forward and the corresponding words address a female deity.

pulisa-send-animals-ahead.title: Drive the bull and ewe ahead
pulisa-send-animals-ahead.description: The bull and ewe are driven in front of the two human substitutes.

tunnawiya-prepare-black-animals.title: Bring the black animals
tunnawiya-prepare-black-animals.description: A black sheep, piglet and puppy are prepared; the prescribed sexes depend on the patient.

tunnawiya-set-out-black-clothes.title: Set out the black clothes
tunnawiya-set-out-black-clothes.description: Black clothing, shoes and wool are supplied for the patient.

tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.title: Offer bread and wine
tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.description: Thin bread, groats and wine are offered at the riverbank or spring.
tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.matchRule: Break thin bread and pour wine at a water source; the riverbank and spring remain distinct occurrences.

tunnawiya-address-riverbank-goddess.title: Address the riverbank Mother-goddess
tunnawiya-address-riverbank-goddess.description: Tunnawiya asks the riverbank Mother-goddess to cleanse the patient with clay.

tunnawiya-collect-clay.title: Take clay from a water source
tunnawiya-collect-clay.description: Tunnawiya takes clay first from the riverbank and then from the spring.
tunnawiya-collect-clay.matchRule: Take clay from a named water source; preserve riverbank and spring as distinct locations on the occurrences.

tunnawiya-build-reed-hut.title: Build the reed shelter
tunnawiya-build-reed-hut.description: A reed shelter is built beside the river, away from tilled land.

tunnawiya-make-clay-figures.title: Make clay tongues and oxen
tunnawiya-make-clay-figures.description: Tunnawiya models twelve tongue shapes and two oxen from the collected clay.

tunnawiya-dress-in-black.title: Dress the patient in black
tunnawiya-dress-in-black.description: At first light the patient puts on the black clothes.

tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep.title: Hold a black sheep over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep.description: Tunnawiya holds a black sheep over the patient while reciting.

tunnawiya-hold-piglet.title: Hold the piglet over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-piglet.description: A piglet is held over the patient with its own incantation.

tunnawiya-hold-puppy.title: Hold the puppy over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-puppy.description: A puppy is held over the patient with its own incantation.

tunnawiya-hold-clay-tongue.title: Hold a clay tongue over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-clay-tongue.description: A clay tongue is lifted over the patient with a prescribed incantation.

tunnawiya-melt-figures.title: Melt the wax and tallow figures
tunnawiya-melt-figures.description: After holding the figures over the patient, Tunnawiya melts them.

tunnawiya-wash-hands-wine.title: Wash the hands with wine
tunnawiya-wash-hands-wine.description: The patient rises and washes the hands with wine.

tunnawiya-wash-with-water.title: Wash the patient with water
tunnawiya-wash-with-water.description: The patient washes with water while Tunnawiya continues the incantation.

tunnawiya-remove-coloured-wool.title: Take blue and red wool off the patient
tunnawiya-remove-coloured-wool.description: Tunnawiya removes blue and red wool from the patient while speaking.

tunnawiya-strip-black-clothes.title: Slit the black shirt
tunnawiya-strip-black-clothes.description: Tunnawiya cuts the black shirt down its length and removes the dark garments.

tunnawiya-smash-empty-pot.title: Smash the empty pot
tunnawiya-smash-empty-pot.description: An empty pot is waved over the patient and smashed.

tunnawiya-bathe-over-figure.title: Bathe over a clay figure
tunnawiya-bathe-over-figure.description: A clay figure is placed beneath the patient’s feet as the patient bathes.

tunnawiya-comb-down.title: Comb the patient downward
tunnawiya-comb-down.description: Maidservants draw boxwood combs downward over the patient.

tunnawiya-release-into-river.title: Send the used objects into the river
tunnawiya-release-into-river.description: The combs, clothing and other used objects are sent into the river.

tunnawiya-burn-small-animals.title: Burn the piglet and puppy
tunnawiya-burn-small-animals.description: The puppy and piglet are taken to uncultivated ground and burned.

tunnawiya-pass-through-gate.title: Pass beneath the wooden gate
tunnawiya-pass-through-gate.description: The patient leaves beneath the alanza-wood gate as Tunnawiya speaks.

tunnawiya-take-cow-by-horn.title: Take the cow by its horn
tunnawiya-take-cow-by-horn.description: Tunnawiya takes hold of a cow by its horn to begin a fertility comparison.

tunnawiya-wish-for-offspring.title: Ask for offspring through the cow analogy
tunnawiya-wish-for-offspring.description: Addressing the Sun-god, Tunnawiya likens the patient’s hoped-for descendants to a fertile cow’s increase.

tunnawiya-touch-fruit-tree.title: Take hold of a fruit-bearing tree
tunnawiya-touch-fruit-tree.description: Tunnawiya takes hold of a fruit-bearing tree.

tunnawiya-wish-by-tree.title: Ask for descendants through the tree analogy
tunnawiya-wish-by-tree.description: Tunnawiya addresses the Sun-god and compares descendants to the fruit on a tree.

tunnawiya-libate-sun-god.title: Pour wine for the Sun-god
tunnawiya-libate-sun-god.description: The patient pours a libation and calls on the Sun-god to keep the cleansing effective.

tunnawiya-return-river-offering.title: Offer bread again at the riverbank
tunnawiya-return-river-offering.description: Tunnawiya returns to the riverbank with bread and groats.
